summary: Proparacaine hydrochloride is a rapid-acting ester-type topical anesthetic used in ophthalmology for short procedures such as tonometry, gonioscopy, removal of corneal foreign bodies, and minor corneal/conjunctival surgery. Onset is within seconds and lasts about 10-20 minutes. It is for in-office procedural use only - prolonged or repeated patient self-use causes severe corneal damage.
indications: Corneal anesthesia of short duration for tonometry
Removal of corneal foreign bodies and sutures
Short corneal and conjunctival surgical procedures

dosage.d: 1-2 drops (single instillations) in each eye before procedure
1 drop in each eye every 5-10 minutes for 5-7 doses
Same as adult; instill 1-2 drops as directed by ophthalmologist

admin: Topical ocular use only - never inject and never prescribe for home/self use
Instill into the conjunctival sac; avoid touching dropper to eye
Solution should be clear to straw-colored - discard if it darkens
Patient should avoid rubbing or touching the eye until anesthesia wears off
Protect the anesthetized eye from dust and bacterial contamination
moa: An ester-type local anesthetic that reversibly blocks sodium channels on corneal and conjunctival sensory nerve endings, preventing the initiation and conduction of nerve impulses and thereby abolishing the sensation of pain. Onset is within seconds; duration is short (about 10-20 minutes).

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to proparacaine or any component of the preparation
relative: History of allergy to ester-type local anesthetics
Cardiac disease and hyperthyroidism (theoretical, with systemic absorption)
monitor: Signs of corneal toxicity or persistent epithelial defects with repeated use

preg: Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted. It is unknown whether proparacaine can cause fetal harm. Use in a pregnant woman only if clearly needed; systemic exposure from a single topical dose is minimal.
lact: It is not known whether proparacaine is excreted in human milk. Exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman; systemic absorption from single topical ocular use is low.
renal: No dose adjustment required; systemic absorption is negligible and elimination does not depend on renal function.
hepatic: No specific adjustment; the ester is rapidly hydrolyzed by plasma and tissue esterases (cholinesterase).

interactions.diagnostics: Topical anesthesia may transiently alter corneal sensitivity tests and tear function tests (e.g., Schirmer)

common: Transient stinging, burning, or redness on instillation
serious: Corneal epithelial toxicity / softening and erosion with repeated or prolonged use
rare: Local allergic contact dermatitis of eyelids
Diffuse epithelial keratitis with grey ground-glass appearance

monitoring: Inspect cornea for epithelial defects if repeated doses are given
Do not allow take-home use - monitor for signs of topical anesthetic abuse (poorly healing corneal ulcer)
counsel: This numbing drop is for use in the clinic only - never take the bottle home or use it to relieve eye pain
Your eye will be numb for about 10-20 minutes - do not rub or touch the eye
Protect the eye from dust and bright light until sensation returns
Report any prolonged pain, severe redness, or vision changes
pk: Very rapid - corneal anesthesia within ~13-30 seconds
Not well characterized; rapidly hydrolyzed by esterases
Refrigerate (2-8 C) per many labels / store as directed; protect from light; keep tightly closed; discard if discolored
pearls: Strictly procedural - chronic patient self-administration causes severe sight-threatening keratopathy and is a recognized form of anesthetic abuse
Faster onset and less initial stinging than tetracaine for routine ophthalmic use
Ester anesthetic - cross-reactivity possible with other ester agents (e.g., tetracaine, benzocaine)
Useful for tonometry and rapid foreign-body removal
missed: Not applicable - administered by a clinician at the time of an eye procedure, not on a scheduled dosing regimen.
overdose: Systemic toxicity from topical ocular use is extremely unlikely. Inadvertent large systemic exposure of ester local anesthetics could cause CNS excitation/seizures then depression and cardiovascular effects - manage supportively with airway, oxygen, and seizure control. Ocular overuse/abuse causes severe corneal epithelial breakdown requiring discontinuation and ophthalmologic care.
